leading_positions.synthesis: Four members prefer optical lattice clocks for Katori and Ye, each with a two-name configuration, and cite independent agreement of Sr, Yb and Hg clocks at the 1e-18 level, the clean credit, and the tests of relativity, constants and dark matter. They differ on framing: Kroll stresses precision as the achievement, Lindroth wants the citation to say what is learned about nature, and Olsson and Pearce ask that the citation be built around the magic-wavelength lattice clock and that early-demonstration dates and 1e-18 values be checked against the record. Danielsson, Johansson and Mehlig ranked B041 seventh in the opening round. Of these, Danielsson and Mehlig list it among their round-1 alternatives, and Johansson names it as his first alternative.

Eriksson and Mehlig prefer topological insulators with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, a theory pair plus the first experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells. They agree that band topology is a new organising principle, that the field is mature after roughly two decades of independent confirmation, and that it follows the 2016 prize without duplicating it. Both accept that Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (HgTe proposal) and Fu (3D) are outside the credited names. Eriksson and Mehlig also differ in how they rank B046, with Mehlig treating it as a reason to wait and Eriksson as a strong alternative.

Danielsson prefers topological insulators with Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan, so that the prize covers theory, the 2D experiment and the 3D ARPES discovery of real materials. He agrees on the science with the Kane-Mele-Molenkamp group but would drop Mele for Hasan, and says he could live with the Kane-Mele-Molenkamp trio while asking that the committee decide the question explicitly. The two B032 configurations differ by exactly one name.

Johansson alone prefers circuit quantum electrodynamics for Blais, Wallraff and Schoelkopf, as strong, tunable coupling of a single microwave photon to a superconducting artificial atom. He discloses that he is the member closest to this field and invites the committee to discount his ranking. Kroll ranked B031 third in the opening round and Mehlig eighth, and Mehlig has said he would not defend it on timing grounds. Neither Kroll nor Mehlig prefers it in round 1.

areas_of_agreement: All eight members' preferred configurations are single-part prizes, and all three of B041, B032 and B031 are described by their supporters as having a stable, independently confirmed interpretation.

Members across the B041 and B032 camps name each other's candidate as a main alternative: Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce name B032 as an alternative, and Danielsson, Eriksson and Mehlig name B041 or B046 among theirs. Every member's alternatives include B032 or B041.

Several members, including Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce, say that credit for B041 is cleaner than for B032, while Danielsson, Eriksson and Mehlig acknowledge that B032 attribution is the main weakness of that candidate.

Members who comment on B046 (Danielsson, Eriksson, Mehlig, Kroll) treat it as scientifically strong but premature because the pairing mechanism is unresolved, and Eriksson and Mehlig place it as an alternative and not as co-equal to B032.

Several members note that precise facts quoted from memory (clock uncertainties, priority chronology of Kane-Mele versus Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, early lattice-clock demonstrations) have not been checked against the record, and want them verified before any citation is drafted.
scientific_disputes: Whether optical lattice clocks count as a discovery that changes our picture of nature or as an outstanding instrument and metrology achievement. Lindroth, Olsson and Danielsson raise this explicitly, and Danielsson says no deviation from known physics has yet been seen.

Whether a conceptual advance such as a new classification of phases (B032) should weigh more than a mature measurement capability (B041), as Eriksson and Mehlig argue, or less, as Kroll and Lindroth argue.

Whether circuit QED is a distinct physical discovery (strong single-photon coupling and dispersive readout) or mainly an enabling architecture for quantum computing, and how distinct it is from the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits.
Whether the pairing mechanism and twist-angle disorder in magic-angle graphene (B046) are open questions that should bar a prize now.
attribution_disputes: B032: Eriksson and Mehlig name Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, while Danielsson names Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (HgTe proposal) and Fu (3D with Kane) are outside every proposed trio, and Hasan's 3D ARPES priority against other ARPES groups is unverified. Mele is Kane's co-author on the founding Z2 papers.

B041: Katori and Ye are the two credited names in all four preferring configurations, but Olsson, Lindroth and Pearce note that PTB, SYRTE, JILA-adjacent groups, Takamoto and other lattice-clock groups made contributions, and Olsson and Lindroth ask for the dates of the first strontium lattice clock and first 1e-18 evaluations to be verified. Lindroth leaves a third name open, while Olsson would hold at two names.

B031: Girvin and Huang co-authored the 2004 proposal and the Yale and ETH experiments were shared, so the Blais, Wallraff, Schoelkopf cut is contested, though Johansson defends it as the cut the field itself makes.

B033: Halzen and Karle are the two names, but AMANDA and IceCube founders and leaders, including Gaisser and Kowalski mentioned in discussion, are outside them, and the collaboration has hundreds of members. Pearce, who ranked B033 first in opening, lists it as an alternative, not as a preferred part.
Comb overlap: Ye's contribution to frequency combs (2005 prize) is raised as a possible overlap, and Lindroth and Olsson would word the B041 citation around the lattice clock only.
maturity_disputes: B041: whether the still-pending redefinition of the second should be a condition for completeness (Mehlig, Kroll raise it) or whether, as Olsson says, the physics and inter-laboratory agreement already exist.

B041 versus earlier prizes: Danielsson, Mehlig and Eriksson see overlap or a third metrology prize as a harder sell, while Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce say the many-atom magic-wavelength scheme is distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes.
B031: whether a circuit prize so soon after 2025 is a timing issue and not a merit issue. Johansson frames it as a timing argument, and Mehlig and Kroll cite it as a reason for caution.
B033: Danielsson and Lindroth call source identification partial (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068) and think the case would be firmer in a few years.
B046: the unresolved superconducting mechanism leads Eriksson, Mehlig, Danielsson and Kroll to treat it as premature for now.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson (prefers B031): leads the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology, works in the same Chalmers superconducting-circuit community as the B031 candidates, and asks the committee to decide whether disclosure or recusal is needed. He reports no personal connection to Blais, Wallraff or Schoelkopf.

Pearce (chair): member of the PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur collaborations, flags field proximity to B033 (his opening first choice, now an alternative), and reports no direct tie to Halzen or Karle and no conflict for B041.
Eriksson (prefers B032): flags field proximity to electronic-structure theory of topological and moire materials as a bias in favour of B032 and B046, with no known connection to the credited names.

Kroll (prefers B041): connected through his PhD advisor Svanberg and a stay in John Hall's laboratory to the laser-spectroscopy community, with no direct collaboration with Katori or Ye. For B031 his WACQT role overlaps institutionally with Chalmers and Johansson.

Mehlig and Olsson: note a shared Gothenburg environment with Johansson without known collaboration. Lindroth reports a mild user relationship with XFEL sources (B005), which is not in her preferred configuration.
questions_for_round2: For B041, what has the lattice clock already taught us about nature (relativistic redshift over millimetres, bounds on varying constants or dark matter), and can the citation state that and distinguish it from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, so that members who ranked it seventh (Danielsson, Johansson, Mehlig) can say whether it is a scientific objection or an overlap objection?

For B032, which three-person configuration is defensible: Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, or Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan? What do the priority chronologies show for Kane-Mele against Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and for Hasan's 3D ARPES against other groups, and would a citation tied to the 2D quantum spin Hall state avoid the 3D attribution problem?

Does the committee treat attribution cleanliness (B041, two names) or conceptual novelty (B032) as the weightier criterion when they point in different directions, and which members would accept each as a fallback, given that B041 and B032 are each other's most frequent alternative?

Can members verify, from the historical record and expert reports, who first realised the strontium lattice clock and first reached 1e-18 uncertainty, and whether Katori and Ye are sufficient without a third lattice-clock name?

For B031, is circuit QED a physical discovery distinct from the 2025 macroscopic quantum tunnelling prize, and does Johansson's disclosed proximity call for recusal or only for discounting his ranking? Would Kroll and Mehlig, who ranked it, accept it if timing were not an issue?

Does the committee want to keep B033 and B046 as candidates for a later year (source identification for neutrinos, pairing mechanism for twisted graphene), and does any member wish to argue for either as a current part?
summary.chair_observation: Support is split across three single-part preferences: B041 has four explicit supporters, B032 has three split across two trios, and B031 has one. The opening support for B041 was broad but shallow, and for B032 narrow but deep, so the round-1 counts alone do not settle the matter. The sharpest open issues are the one-name difference inside B032, whether lattice clocks overlap earlier metrology prizes, and Johansson's disclosed proximity to B031. Several facts quoted from memory still need checking before any citation is drafted. As chair I have a preference for B041 and have tried to state the B032 and B031 cases in their supporters' terms.
